issue.title: nacos-client 3.2.3: sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory warning from shaded Netty still reproduces on JDK 25

llm_context.input_title: nacos-client 3.2.3: sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory warning from shaded Netty still reproduces on JDK 25
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: The nacos-client library shades gRPC and Netty dependencies. On JDK 25, Netty's internal PlatformDependent0 class attempts to use sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory for off-heap memory allocation, which triggers a terminal deprecation warning on startup.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The root cause is that the shaded version of Netty (packaged inside nacos-client via gRPC shading) uses sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory for direct memory access/allocation. In JDK 25, this method is terminally deprecated, causing the JVM to emit a warning when it is accessed. Since the dependency is shaded inside nacos-client, the warning points directly to the nacos-client JAR. Note that the exact pom.xml or shading configuration files are INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE in the retrieved codebase chunks.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect Shaded Dependencies
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect the root pom.xml and client/pom.xml to identify the exact versions of io.grpc and io.netty being shaded into the nacos-client artifact.

step_by_step_plan.title: Upgrade Shaded Netty/gRPC Versions
step_by_step_plan.description: Upgrade the shaded io.grpc and io.netty dependencies to versions that support JDK 25 and avoid using terminally deprecated sun.misc.Unsafe methods, or configure the system property 'io.netty.noUnsafe=true' during client initialization.

step_by_step_plan.title: Verify Warning Absence on JDK 25
step_by_step_plan.description: Run the nacos-client initialization code on JDK 25 and verify that no terminal deprecation warnings regarding sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory are printed to standard error.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Shading is the process of renaming and packaging a dependency (and its transitive dependencies) inside another jar file to avoid classpath conflicts.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: It allows library developers to bundle specific versions of third-party libraries (like Netty or gRPC) without forcing the users of the library to use those exact same versions in their own applications.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The warning comes from com.alibaba.nacos.shaded.io.grpc.netty..., which is a shaded version of Netty bundled inside nacos-client. To fix the warning, Nacos must upgrade the underlying dependency that is being shaded.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The sun.misc.Unsafe class provides low-level, unsafe mechanisms (like direct off-heap memory allocation) that bypass JVM safety checks. Modern JDK versions (like JDK 25) are terminally deprecating and removing these APIs.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Developers must transition away from sun.misc.Unsafe to ensure their applications remain compatible with future Java releases and do not crash or emit warnings on startup.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Netty's PlatformDependent0 class uses Unsafe::allocateMemory for high-performance off-heap buffer allocation. On JDK 25, this triggers a terminal deprecation warning, requiring an upgrade to a Netty version that uses modern JDK APIs or handles the deprecation gracefully.

common_pitfalls: Manually editing shaded class files instead of upgrading the parent dependency in the build configuration (e.g., Maven pom.xml).
Assuming the warning can be silenced by standard Java logging configurations, as JVM-level Unsafe warnings are printed directly to standard error by the runtime.
Upgrading only the direct gRPC dependency without ensuring that the shaded Netty transitive dependency is also updated to a version compatible with JDK 25.
